what_it_does: As chip makers shrink to 2-nanometer sizes (the cutting edge), they face a challenge: the memory cells themselves can't get much smaller without losing reliability. This paper describes a design approach that works around that limit by making the circuits around the memory cells more efficient. Using 2nm nanosheet transistors—which let more current flow for a given size—the team was able to pack 2x more memory bits per supporting circuit. This means denser, faster memory that doesn't compromise on reliability.
